decisions.question: Which one class does the v0.15.1 change request take (hsdd-intake Process step 4: local, cross-node, new-capability, structural)?

options.label: local
options.consequence: One hsdd-phase-plan append on one leaf-parent. Cannot hold a change that restates guarantees of five contracts and ADR-003 and reaches six nodes.

options.label: cross-node
options.consequence: hsdd-adr and hsdd-contract steps first, then the affected nodes' specs and phase plans, then reconcile; the existing node and contract set stays.

options.label: new-capability
options.consequence: A graft under an existing parent. Needs a node that does not exist; v0.15.1 needs none (see the shape decision).

options.label: structural
options.consequence: Stop with options. Requires the tree's shape to be wrong for the change, which the shape decision finds it is not.

decisions.why: v0.15.1 rewrites the startup barrier (Spec §3.13), adds scope timing (§7.2), makes the write chain the unit an error terminates (§10.2), sends shell subscriber errors to the listen zone (§10.2 principle 5), names the runtime name-check fields (§4.3) and adds a Flutter module wrapper (§7.3). Those land on topology-dsl, bus-api, bus-testing, navigation-api and flutter-binding, on ADR-003's item 2 and item 6, and on the specs or plans of nidana, nidana.model, nidana.runtime, nidana.navigation, nidana.flutter and nidana.integration. No single leaf-parent holds that, and no new node is needed.

decisions.question: Does v0.15.1 make the tree's shape wrong (a node or contract that should not exist, or one that is missing), which would make the change structural?

options.label: Shape holds
options.consequence: Every landing fits an existing node and contract: the barrier's topic storage and fan-out inside nidana.runtime, the connection order computed there, NidanaModule in nidana.flutter's package and flutter-binding@v1.

options.label: Split nidana.runtime into topic storage and operator engine
options.consequence: Guide §6.1's machinery as its own node joined by an internal contract whose fixtures import lib/src/, which ADR-001 item 2 forbids, so it could never be stable; reopens nidana.runtime D1.

options.label: Graft a Flutter module-wrapper node
options.consequence: A child for one widget of the existing adapter package, with no contract boundary of its own, against ADR-002 item 3's one owning node per package.

decisions.why: Guide §6.1 has a Dart bus keep its own topic storage and fan-out, or wrap each subject, and still use RxDart for operators, so ADR-002's stated signal for splitting the runtime (a v1 requirement for a second engine) is not met and nidana.runtime D1's reasons against a split stand. Spec Appendix A.8 places NidanaModule in the Flutter adapter package, which nidana.flutter owns. The writers-before-readers connection order is a computation over the bootstrap activations' graph; if bus-api wants it as a pure function, topology-ir@v1's Versioning admits a new analysis function compatibly, which changes no contract set. The Guide and the Spec give one option a stated reason, so this is not a tree-shape run-stop. Signal that would change it: a v1 requirement for a second engine, or an owner request for a separately versioned module-binding package.

decisions.question: Guide §6.3 'Name every transformer' now says that on Dart re-activation compares transformers and a closure equals only itself, so the second activation of a topology with inline lambdas throws; bus-api@v1 G23 (DEC-167) counts definitions equal under topology-ir equality, closure bodies included, as one declaration. Is this a landing, and where does it route?

options.label: Landing, routed to bus-api with the Guide's reading recommended
options.consequence: The bus-api handoff decides G23; comparing the plan's functions and seeds catches captured-value differences the IR cannot see, at the cost that a topology with inline lambdas is never idempotent; consequences for page holder counts and navResolver are named.

options.label: No landing: the Guide is informative and Spec §3.9 did not change
options.consequence: DEC-167 stays and so does its silent-sharing hazard (two instances capturing different values share one handle); the divergence from v0.15.1's Guide goes unrecorded.

options.label: Landing, decided in the record
options.consequence: The intake would settle a contract guarantee, which hsdd-intake never writes.

decisions.chosen: Landing, routed to bus-api with the Guide's reading recommended
decisions.why: The step's decision policy treats a reason stated by the Guide as deciding, and v0.15.1's Guide reads Spec §3.9 for Dart explicitly. The runtime fact is measured: two evaluations of one closure expression are unequal. DEC-167 itself named the signal that would change it (two different closures silently sharing a handle), which the Guide's reading prevents. The intake writes no contract, so H3 decides. Signal that would favor keeping IR equality: a v1 flow that must re-activate a topology rebuilt with inline lambdas; page scopes avoid this through holder counts that activate once per id.

decisions.question: Spec §7.3's Flutter row and Appendix A.8 name a NidanaModule wrapper widget beside the route observer; flutter-binding@v1 has only ModuleRoutes and ModuleScopeObserver. How does the intake route it?

options.label: Route to flutter-binding, recommend adding it
options.consequence: A compatible addition under flutter-binding's Versioning ('a new widget'); binds module scope for apps on go_router or any Router-based setup whose routes may carry no names; one more widget in nidana.flutter.6 or a small appended phase.

options.label: Route to flutter-binding, recommend leaving it out
options.consequence: The Spec's 'or' allows the route observer alone; an app whose routes carry no names keeps no module binding in v1.

options.label: Graft a node for it
options.consequence: Rejected by the shape decision: a widget of an existing package.

decisions.chosen: Route to flutter-binding, recommend adding it
decisions.why: Spec Appendix A.8 lists the wrapper among what the Flutter adapter provides, Guide Appendix B.3 names NidanaModule(topology, child) for Flutter, and flutter-binding Refinement 1 already leaves apps on Router-based setups to implement NavigationRouter themselves while ModuleScopeObserver needs named routes. The step deciding it runs the experiment. Signal against: the experiment showing a wrapper cannot hold the count above zero across a shell route's transitions within the grace period.

decisions.question: Spec §4.3's runtime row now names variant, payload type, sensitivity, deduplication and replay size as the fields a second declaration is compared on; bus-api@v1 G7 also compares tracing. How does the intake route this?

options.label: Route to bus-api as a question, recommend keeping tracing, marked would_upstream
options.consequence: G7 stays stricter than the Spec's list, which is silent on tracing; one tracing flag per subject keeps observer gating (bus-api G30) independent of access order.

options.label: Recommend dropping tracing to match the list
options.consequence: Two declarations differing only in tracing share a subject, and whether observers see its envelopes depends on which declaration published.

options.label: No landing
options.consequence: Leaves G7's relation to the new Spec text unstated.

decisions.chosen: Route to bus-api as a question, recommend keeping tracing, marked would_upstream
decisions.why: v0.15.1 adopted DEC-168's request to name the fields but neither lists nor excludes tracing, so G7 does not contradict it. DEC-168's reason for sensitivity (gating cannot recover from mixed flags on one subject) applies to tracing through bus-api G30. The Specification should say which way tracing goes, hence would_upstream.

decisions.question: Guide §6.3 advises an explicit name for each transformer where FunctionRef labels must be stable, because a name derived from Function.toString() differs between compilation modes and is obfuscated. Does topology-dsl or topology-ir change in v1?

options.label: No change; topology-dsl keeps it under Not in v1 and records the Guide's advice
options.consequence: No declaration or projection rule changes; labels stay derived.

options.label: Add an optional name to every combinator and a projection rule
options.consequence: Compatible on topology-dsl (a new optional named parameter) but a change to topology-ir's projection rules, which its Versioning lists as breaking.

decisions.chosen: No change; topology-dsl keeps it under Not in v1 and records the Guide's advice
decisions.why: No v1 consumer compares FunctionRef labels across compilation modes or under --obfuscate: re-activation compares within one process, and nidana.integration D8 keeps the example's transformers public so the JIT catalog equals the AOT graph. Signal that would change it: comparing graphs from obfuscated release builds, which only the runtime devtools root D1 defers to v2 would need.

decisions.question: Guide Appendix C.1's new paragraph has the catalog take an explicit list of topologies and claims where the runtime has no reflection. Is it a landing on the tooling contracts?

options.label: No contract landing; Sources and a D1 note in nidana.tooling.codegen
options.consequence: topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1 stay; D1 records that the Guide now describes its registration library.

options.label: Restate topic-codegen and nidana-checks to say a topology left off the list is checked only at run time
options.consequence: Repeats what nidana.tooling.codegen D1's close-call signal already names; claims are recognized from source by the scan anyway.

decisions.chosen: No contract landing; Sources and a D1 note in nidana.tooling.codegen
decisions.why: The paragraph matches DEC-365's registration library, and the orphan and unreachable-topic analyses it says need the full walk are deferred to v2 by root D1. The scan recognizes claims in source (nidana-checks Refinement 2), so only an unregistered topology escapes, the case D1 already names.

decisions.question: Where does the rejection of a MODULE or PAGE activation before start() (Spec §7.2 Scope timing) live?

options.label: In bus-api only
options.consequence: A BusError variant or the SDK error bus-api's misuse rule names; topology-ir untouched.

options.label: As a new topology-ir finding variant raised through ActivationRejected
options.consequence: Breaking for topology-ir@v1, whose TopologyFinding family is closed (G1, Versioning), for a rule CI cannot check, since the IR does not know when an activation happens relative to start().

decisions.why: Scope timing is a property of the bus's lifecycle, not of the graph; putting it in the IR's findings would version a third contract for no consumer that can use it.

decisions.question: How does ADR-003 change for Spec §10.2 principle 5 (subscriber errors to the listen zone) and §3.13 (first delivery during bootstrap): amended in place, superseded, or left?

options.consequence: One bullet of item 2, a sentence of item 6 and a Consequences bullet change under a dated Amendments entry; ids and Governed by links stay, as ADR-001's three amendments and ADR-003's first did.

options.label: Supersede with ADR-004
options.consequence: A fresh accepted text; every Governed by link of ADR-003 (five nodes, five contracts, many phases) moves to ADR-004.

options.label: Leave ADR-003 and state the zone rule in bus-api only
options.consequence: bus-api would contradict an accepted ADR that governs it.

decisions.chosen: Amend in place; supersede only if item 2 or item 6 is replaced as a whole
decisions.why: The ADR's decision (a zone and a clock as the provider, nidana's own virtual scheduler, RxDart's time operators) stands; only where a subscriber's error goes and when a bootstrap subscription first receives change. hsdd-adr's supersede rule exists so that no stale accepted text is injected; an in-place amendment keeps the text current. The H1 step may still supersede, with its reason.

decisions.question: How do the 64 unshipped phases absorb the change: appended phases, unshipped phases rewritten through hsdd-reconcile, or both; and which skill edits which phase?

options.label: Append only
options.consequence: Existing phases keep v0.15.0 scopes their gates no longer pass against the new fixtures; appended phases undo them, a wasted review window per reworked slice.

options.label: Rewrite every plan through one hsdd-reconcile sweep, as S53 did
options.consequence: One step, but reconcile has no sizing, tier or replay-schedule process for a design change such as the runtime's start(); its charter is draining entries.

options.label: Phase-plan append mode rewriting in place for runtime, flutter and integration; final reconcile sweep for citation-only plans; insert rule
options.consequence: Three phase-plan steps that rewrite unshipped phases in place and append only unowned work, each followed by a reconcile; the final reconcile sweeps nidana.model, nidana.navigation, nidana.tooling.codegen and nidana.tooling.lint; a node whose guarantees change beyond citations gets its own phase-plan step.

decisions.chosen: Phase-plan append mode rewriting in place for runtime, flutter and integration; final reconcile sweep for citation-only plans; insert rule
decisions.why: hsdd-intake routes a cross-node change to hsdd-phase-plan on each node, in append mode when it has phases; append mode forbids renumbering and rewriting a shipped phase, and no phase has shipped (no hsdd/verify/), so unshipped phases can be rewritten in place with their ids. phase-plan owns sizes, tiers and the --guarantee lists the new fixtures change, and a phase that names the record in its Scope lets hsdd-checkpoint list it under Produced and close the record. The owner's 'make sure everything is aligned, all decisions, all artifacts' rules out append only. Close call against the S53-style sweep; signal that would favor it: a delta of wording only, which holds for the four swept nodes.

decisions.question: Are the citation-only touches of contracts and ADRs listed unconditionally, or with skip rules evaluated after the content handoffs?

decisions.why: Which contracts take a new version is the contract steps' classification (DEC-688), not the intake's, so the record cannot know which touches will be needed; a rule written now keeps the routing auditable.

decisions.question: In what order do the handoffs run, ending with an hsdd-reconcile that drains every pending section?

options.label: ADR-003, contracts producer-first, citation touches, node touches and plans producer-first with a reconcile after each plan, root last, final reconcile
options.consequence: Each step reads its producers' settled text; flutter's and integration's plans read bus-api's Delivery after the runtime's plan has been reconciled into it.

options.label: Contracts first, ADR-003 after
options.consequence: bus-api would state a subscriber-error zone that the accepted ADR-003 contradicts.

options.label: One reconcile at the end only
options.consequence: nidana.flutter's and nidana.integration's plans would read Delivery paragraphs before the runtime plan's amends reach them.

decisions.chosen: ADR-003, contracts producer-first, citation touches, node touches and plans producer-first with a reconcile after each plan, root last, final reconcile
decisions.why: Producer-first, as the run did in stages 2 to 6. ADR-003 governs five of the contracts. topology-dsl precedes bus-api, which binds its live suite; bus-api precedes bus-testing, navigation-api and flutter-binding, which consume it; flutter-binding is last because it binds navigation-api's executor suite. Each leaf-parent's spec touch precedes its plan, a reconcile follows each plan as in stage 6, nidana.tooling follows its children, and the root comes last because it embeds the children's blocks and names their phases (precedent S26, S47).

notes_for_orchestrator: Record: hsdd/management/2026-10-20-intake-ref-arch-v0-15-1.md. Handoffs in order: H1 hsdd-adr ADR-003; H2 to H6 hsdd-contract topology-dsl, bus-api, bus-testing, navigation-api, flutter-binding; H7a to H7i conditional hsdd-contract citation touches (topic-model, topology-dsl, topology-ir, bus-api, bus-testing, navigation-api, flutter-binding, topic-codegen, nidana-checks); H8a to H8c conditional hsdd-adr citation touches (ADR-001, ADR-002, ADR-003); H9 spec nidana.model; H10 spec nidana.runtime; H11 phase-plan nidana.runtime; H12 reconcile; H13 spec nidana.navigation; H14 spec nidana.flutter; H15 phase-plan nidana.flutter; H16 reconcile; H17 to H19 spec nidana.tooling.codegen, nidana.tooling.lint, nidana.tooling; H20 spec nidana.integration; H21 phase-plan nidana.integration; H22 spec root; H23 final reconcile with gate --final.

Expected classifications, for the contract steps to confirm: bus-api's changes look breaking under its own list (a delivery rule, the timing of first delivery, which operation throws what), so expect the next version under DEC-688; topology-dsl's write-chain rule may read as a clarification of 'ends that sink' or as a change to the Errors and lineage rules its list calls breaking; flutter-binding's NidanaModule is compatible by its list, scope timing touches its cases and example; navigation-api's changes look textual; bus-testing depends on H1's zone decision.
The step section placed the RxDart, RxJS, RxKotlin, RxSwift bullet in Spec §3.6; in v0.15.1 it is in §3.3 (Ordering Guarantees). The record cites §3.3.

would_upstream decisions read against v0.15.1. Contradicted, so landings: DEC-166 (barrier held only publishes), DEC-158 for a subscription made during bootstrap (adopted for a running bus by Spec §2.1), DEC-167 (by Guide §6.3). Adopted: DEC-032 (Spec §2.1, §3.3; Guide §6.1, §6.5), DEC-168 except tracing (Spec §4.3), DEC-249 (Spec §7.3 Flutter row), DEC-365 (Guide Appendix C.1). Left open: the other 31 (DEC-018, 026, 027, 028, 029, 030, 052, 053, 061, 078, 085, 098, 099, 122, 123, 124, 134, 142, 144, 150, 159, 169, 217, 219, 221, 247, 253, 257, 273, 274, 586); DEC-253 meets L6, and Spec §7.2's new hydration sentence supports DEC-586's reading.

The gate requires a contract's file name to equal its id, so a new version lives in the same file, with v1 named in its Versioning migration note; @v1 citations then pass the per-step gate and show as stale-version warnings under --final, which H7, H8, the spec touches and H23 clear.

No experiment ran in this step: the runtime facts the routing rests on are already measured (two closure evaluations unequal in function-ref-derivation/output.txt; the replay microtask in rxdart-sync-subjects/; the synchronous topology read path in bus-api-amendment/). H1, H3, H6 and H10 are told to run experiments for the facts their decisions need.

No OQ was minted. Recommendations the record hands to steps, not decisions taken here: G23 compares the plan's functions (H3); tracing stays in G7, marked would_upstream (H3); NidanaModule is added (H6); explicit transformer names stay out of v1 (H2); the scope-timing rejection stays inside bus-api (H3).
Produced is empty. Phases that H11, H15 and H21 rewrite or append name the record in their Scope, so hsdd-checkpoint will list them and close the record only when they ship.
